newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy shares fade to close mixed, awaiting news.
newsitem.headline: Italy shares fade to close mixed, awaiting news.

text.p: Italian shares faded after rising in the afternoon to end mixed on Monday as the market adjusted positions ahead of preliminary inflation data for January from Turin and Trieste due at 1630 GMT today and nine other sample cities on Tuesday.
Traded volumes picked up after a morning pause for breath but deaslers noted that on Wall Street, Dow industrials lost ground on profit-taking.

Dealers were also looking to announcement from Olivetti whose stock was suspended for the session. The group was widely expected to announce after the market close the sale of its loss-making PC division.
The All-share Mibtel index closed up 0.24 percent at 12,334 bu the Mib30 blue chip index was off 0.08 percent at 18,470.
U.S. bonds and currency markets were not traded because of the Martin Luther King Jr federal holiday.
After an early pause, interest in Milan had picked up in the afternoon. "When it looked like the market was just not set to give way the really keen buyers got back in," one dealer said.
Italian bond futures and the lira were again strong today.
Telecoms were fairly well sought. "They are always attractive to retail investors," one trader said.
Telecoms holding Stet was up 0.53 percent at 7,950 lire after Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi confirmed at the weekend Stet would be privatised by the year end.
Telecom Italia was off 0.19 percent at 4,850 but mobile phone operator TIM was 0.12 percent up at 4,875 lire.

Financial holding Gemina rose sharply, up 4.16 percent at 929 lire but off session highs at 948. Dealers said gains were due to repositioning linked to spin-off of industrial assets into new company HPI.
Energy group ENI put on 0.43 percent to 9,115 lire but Fiat lost 0.91 percent to 5,135 lire.
